newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks extend losses in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks extend losses in moderate trade.

text.p: Thai stocks extended losses for the ninth consecutive session on Tuesday as market sentiment continued to be weighed down by political uncertaintiy and a poor economic outlook, brokers said.
The SET index retreated 4.29 points to close at 982.03 on moderate 4.53 billion baht turnover. Declines led advances 203 to 129. The SET-50 index fell 0.34 point to 74.44.
"Foreigners remained net sellers and banks and finance firms were the targets. The market got another bit of bad news that Morgan Stanley cut Thailand's weighting," a broker at Union Securities said.
"The Morgan Stanley report could be a bearish factor tomorrow," he said.

Morgan Stanley said it cut Thailand's weighting to 6.5 percent from 9.0 percent in its model portfolio in response to expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates which will likely lead to a short-term weakness in Southeast Asian markets.
Brokers said investors also worried that Standard & Poor's may downgrade Thai long-term debt ratings soon which would deal a heavy blow to the market.
They dismissed a tax package announced by Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan on Tuesday as a repeat of previously stated measures which would fail to shore up sentiment.
The dominant bank and finance counters led trading activities, retreating 0.72 and 0.21 percent respectively. Eight of the 10 most active issues came from the two sectors.

Thai Farmers Bank shed two baht to 161, Krung Thai lost one to 98.50, Bangkok Bank fell two to 206, and National Finance retreated two to 64.50. Siam Commercial Bank gained four baht to 236 and General Finance rose one to 54.
